newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil under premium and futures pressure.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil under premium and futures pressure.

text.p: NWE gas oil slipped on Monday as premiums lost ground and IPE futures weakened.
February IPE gas oil, which expires on Wednesday, closed $2.00 a tonne lower at $188.25 having tracked U.S gasoline for much of the day.
Heating oil was slow, particuarly in the barge sector where anticipation of a squeeze by the market long sidelined many.

Traders also said mild weather contributed to the quiet tone. A couple of barges traded, Feb IPE -$1.50 for prompt Rotterdam refinery material in the morning set against buying interest in the afternoon of Feb IPE -$2.
Cargo activity was stiffled by the weaker market.
"People want it to settle down before they come in and buy," said one trader.

Russian gas oil cargoes were talked around March IPE +$5-7 cif NWE although buying interest was broadly notional while FOD was steady to narrowly weaker around March IPE +$6 for second half Feb delivery. Prompt delivery would attract a small premium, dealers said.
Diesel premiums were pegged at between March +$16-18 cif NWE.
